To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
higher OPG concentrations are associated with the presence and extent (but not the composition) of atherosclerosis in HIV-infected and HIV-uninfected persons.

OPG concentrations were higher, but RANKL concentrations lower, among HIV-infected than HIV-uninfected individuals, and OPG, but not RANKL, concentrations were associated with subclinical atherosclerotic burden.
OPG, but not RANKL, concentrations are associated with the presence and extent, respectively, of CVD among HIV-uninfated men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of the OPG/RANKL axis and subclinical atherothrombotic disease in HIV-infected individuals.
the relationship between the OPG/RANKL axis and subclinical atherogenesis in HIV-infected individuals.
the relationship between osteoproteger (OPG) and receptor activator for nuclear factor-kB ligand (Rankl) with subclinical coronary atherosclerosis in HIV infected men.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship of OPG/RANKL with atherosclerotic disease is not clear and that further research is needed.
the role of OPG and RANL in the pathogenesis of CVD in HIV-infected patients remains to be determined.
OPG and RANCL are dysregulated in the HIV infected men and their association with atherosclerotic disease is not the same in HIV infected men as it is in HIV uninfected men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the OPG/RANKL axis may play a role in subclinical atherosclerotic plaque progression in HIV-infected and HIV-uninfected individuals, but this relationship differs by HIV status and by the presence of subclinical atheroma.
OPG is associated with CVD in the HIV population.
the OPG/RANKL axis may play a role in the pathogenesis of CVD among HIV-infected persons, but that the relationship between these biomarkers and CVD may differ by HIV status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between OPG/RANKL and CVD is complex and may be different between HIV-uninfected and HIV-infected individuals.
the association between OPG and RANCL with atherosclerosis is different in the setting of HIV infection.
the relationship of the OPG/RANKL axis to subclinical coronary artery disease is different in HIV-inflicted and uninfected men.
